mainTopic: ברירה in brothers' division, and which animals enter the pen for מעשר בהמה
overview: The amud opens by showing that רבי יוחנן is consistent. Brothers who divide an inheritance are like buyers (אין ברירה), so they return land to each other at יובל, just as they are exempt from מעשר בהמה. The גמרא explains why both rulings were needed. It then challenges the יש ברירה view with a ברייתא about partners who split lambs and a dog, and רב אשי answers that the dog was worth a bit more than one lamb. A new משנה lists five animals that do not enter the pen for מעשר: כלאים, טרפה, יוצא דופן, מחוסר זמן and יתום. The גמרא learns these exclusions from a פסוק about קרבנות and carries them over to מעשר through the גזירה שוה of תחת תחת. It explains why animals involved in עריות or עבודה זרה are still tithed: their disqualification works like a מום, and a מום does not disqualify מעשר. It also explains the dispute about טומטום and אנדרוגינוס. Finally, a ברייתא gives a shorter list of exclusions, and the גמרא begins to explain that opinion, continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is consistent: brothers who divided are buyers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן's ruling on animals matches another ruling of his about land. There he says brothers who divided are like buyers and must return the land at יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning. רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: brothers who divided an inheritance are considered buyers, and they return the land to each other at יובל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ruling of רבי יוחנן to show that his opinion about animals fits a pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each brother's share had been his from the moment the father died (יש ברירה), nothing would need to be returned at יובל. Because רבי יוחנן says they return the land, he must hold that the brothers bought their shares from each other (אין ברירה). That is the same reason they are exempt from מעשר בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning, meaning he is consistent with another ruling of his
Brothers who divided an inheritance
Buyers or purchasers
The Jubilee year, when sold fields return to their original owners

steps.whyThisMatters: This links two separate areas of הלכה, מעשר בהמה and יובל, to one idea: אין ברירה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan follows his own reasoning,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Brothers who divided an inheritance are considered buyers,
phrases.notes: Each brother is treated as if he bought his share from the others.

phrases.english: and they return the land to each other at the Jubilee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's earlier ruling, which appears on the previous amud, that brothers who divided animals are exempt from מעשר בהמה.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן consistently holds brothers who divided are buyers (אין ברירה).
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אסי's report of רבי יוחנן's ruling that divided land returns at יובל.

steps.title: Why both rulings are needed: the animal ruling alone is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the animal ruling alone could not teach us the land ruling. מעשר בהמה has a special requirement that might make it stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both rulings are needed. If he had only taught the animal case, I would say רבי יוחנן ruled that way only there. The reason is that animals are compared to 'your son': just as your firstborn son must clearly be yours, so your cattle and sheep must clearly be yours. But for a field, the Torah only said a SOLD field returns at יובל. An inherited or gifted field would not return.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a צריכותא, explaining why רבי יוחנן had to state both rulings. This step shows why the animal ruling alone would not be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר בהמה requires that the animals be clearly and fully yours, like a firstborn son. So even a slight 'buyer' aspect might exempt them. Land at יובל, though, returns only when it was actually sold. Without the land ruling, we might think inherited land does not count as sold.

keyTerms.meaning: And both are needed (the start of a צריכותא)
Similar to 'your son', a comparison drawn from the verses
Clearly yours
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Inheritance and gift

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is questioning רבי יוחנן's opinion here. It is only explaining why he needed to say the same idea twice.

phrases.english: And both are needed, for if he had taught us only here,
I would say it is in this case that Rabbi Yochanan says it,
because it is similar to 'your son':
just as your son must be clearly yours,
so too your cattle and your sheep must be clearly yours;
but for a field, it is only a sale
that the Torah said should return at the Jubilee,
but inheritance and gift do not!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the second ruling from step 1 was not redundant.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The animal ruling alone could have been limited to מעשר בהמה's special 'clearly yours' requirement, so the land ruling was needed.

steps.title: Why both rulings are needed: the land ruling alone is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The land ruling alone also could not teach the animal ruling. It might only be a stringency, or it might come from the special יובל rule of returning things to how they started.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he had only taught the field case, I would say he ruled that way only to be strict, or because at יובל land goes back to how it was at the beginning. But here, with animals, I would say no. So both rulings are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא by showing why the land ruling alone would not be enough. It concludes that both rulings are necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two reasons are given. First, maybe רבי יוחנן was unsure and ruled strictly (לחומרא). Second, maybe it is a unique feature of יובל that everything returns to its original state (לכתחילה). Neither reason applies to מעשר בהמה, so the animal ruling had to be stated on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: To be strict, ruling stringently because of doubt
Alternatively
To the beginning, meaning restoring things to their original state
It is necessary

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן holds אין ברירה in two places, מעשר בהמה and יובל. Each ruling teaches something the other could not.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only the field,
I would say it is to be strict, or alternatively, to restore things to the beginning,
but here, I would say no;
therefore it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the צריכותא begun in step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both of רבי יוחנן's rulings are needed. Neither one could be learned from the other.

steps.title: A ברייתא about partners who split lambs and a dog
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. When partners divide, one taking ten lambs and the other nine lambs plus a dog, the ten lambs taken against the dog are forbidden as offerings, but the nine taken with the dog are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: An objection was raised: Similarly, partners who divided, where one took ten lambs and the other took nine lambs and a dog. The lambs taken in exchange for the dog are forbidden, and the lambs taken together with the dog are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge by quoting a ברייתא. This step sets up the source, and the next step will explain the attack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה forbids bringing מחיר כלב, something received in exchange for a dog, as an offering. The ברייתא treats all ten lambs as payment for the dog, so all ten are forbidden. The nine that came along with the dog were not payment, so they are permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection, usually from a ברייתא or משנה
Partners
Dog
That are in exchange for
Forbidden, here meaning forbidden as an offering because they are מחיר כלב

phrases.english: They raised an objection: And similarly, partners who divided,
one took ten lambs
and one took nine lambs and a dog:
those taken in exchange for the dog are forbidden,
phrases.notes: Forbidden as offerings because they count as the price of a dog.

phrases.english: those taken with the dog are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from supporting רבי יוחנן to challenging the opposing view, יש ברירה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that holds יש ברירה when partners or brothers divide.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This step sets up the source. The attack itself comes in step 5.

steps.title: If יש ברירה, why are all ten lambs forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that if we hold יש ברירה, only one lamb should be treated as the dog's counterpart, and the rest should be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say יש ברירה, let one of the lambs be chosen as the one against the dog, and let him take it, and the rest should be permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the challenge. Under יש ברירה, the ברייתא should not forbid all ten lambs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dog is worth about one lamb. If ברירה works, we could say afterward that one specific lamb was the dog's exchange, so only that lamb would be forbidden. Since the ברייתא forbids all ten, it seems to hold אין ברירה, which challenges the opposing view.

keyTerms.meaning: Retroactive clarification: a later choice reveals what was true from the start
Let him select
Corresponding to, or against
Let them be permitted

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge is not against רבי יוחנן. He holds אין ברירה, which fits the ברייתא. The challenge is against the view that says יש ברירה.

phrases.english: And if you say there is retroactive designation,
let him select one of them to correspond to the dog
and take it, and these others should be permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenging inference from the ברייתא quoted in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of יש ברירה regarding division between partners or brothers.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under יש ברירה, only one lamb, matching the dog's value, would be forbidden. The ברייתא forbids all ten, which suggests אין ברירה.

steps.title: רב אשי: The Dog Is Worth a Bit More Than One Lamb
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers the question from step 5. The ברייתא is talking about a case where the dog is worth slightly more than one lamb, so its value spreads over all ten lambs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: If all the animals were worth the same, you would be right that only one lamb would count against the dog. But the ברייתא is dealing with a case where they are not equal in value. The dog is worth one lamb plus a little more, and that little bit extra spreads into all the lambs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends the ברייתא against the question from step 5. He shows a case where all ten lambs really are connected to the dog.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was: with יש ברירה, why not set aside just one lamb as the dog's price? רב אשי agrees that this would work if the values were equal. But if the dog is worth more than one lamb, no single lamb can cover it, so a small part of the dog's price ends up mixed into every lamb. That makes all of them forbidden as קרבנות (מחיר כלב).

keyTerms.meaning: "Here, what case are we dealing with?" A phrase that narrows the case to a specific situation
To each other
A tiny amount
Is drawn along and comes; spreads into
A dog

steps.whatToRemember: The ten lambs are forbidden because of the dog's extra value, not because יש ברירה fails. The extra bit is spread over all of them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the sugya. The ברייתא no longer contradicts the יש ברירה view, so that view survives the challenge. רבי יוחנן, who holds אין ברירה (step 1), was never the target of this challenge.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
If they are all equal in value to each other —
indeed so (only one lamb would correspond to the dog),
here, with what are we dealing?
where they are not all equal to each other,
and this dog is worth one (lamb) and a little more,
and this little bit is drawn along into all of them.
phrases.notes: The extra value is divided among all the lambs, so each one holds part of the dog's price.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב אשי אי דשוו כולהו להדדי הכי נמי הכא במאי עסקינן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 5 by narrowing the ברייתא to a specific case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation (אוקימתא): the ברייתא refers to animals of unequal value
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All animals are equal in value, so יש ברירה would assign only one lamb to the dog
steps.terutzMaskana: The dog is worth slightly more than one lamb, so its extra value spreads into all ten lambs and forbids them

steps.title: משנה: Which Animals Are Left Out of the Tithe Pen
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that all animals enter the pen for מעשר בהמה except five types: כלאים, טרפה, יוצא דופן, מחוסר זמן, and יתום.
steps.simpleTranslation: All animals go into the pen to be tithed, except: a mixed-breed animal, a טרפה, an animal born by caesarean, an animal that is too young, and an orphan.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists the animals that are not counted for מעשר בהמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the owner brings all the new animals into a pen and counts them out, and every tenth one becomes holy. This משנה names five kinds of animals that are kept out of that count. These are the same kinds that cannot be brought as קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Pen, where animals are gathered to be counted for tithing
An animal born from two different species
An animal with a fatal defect
An animal born by caesarean section
Too young; under eight days old

phrases.english: MISHNA:
All enter the pen to be tithed,
except for a crossbred animal, and a tereifa,
and one born by caesarean, and one too young, and the orphan.

steps.triggerLanguage: הכל נכנסין לדיר להתעשר חוץ מן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the previous sugya ended
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All animals enter the tithe pen except כלאים, טרפה, יוצא דופן, מחוסר זמן, and יתום

steps.title: Defining an Orphan, and רבי יהושע's Disagreement
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines a יתום as an animal whose mother died or was slaughtered before its birth was finished. רבי יהושע says that if the mother's hide still exists, the animal is not a יתום.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is an orphan? Any animal whose mother died, or was slaughtered, and only afterward finished giving birth. רבי יהושע says: even if the mother was slaughtered, as long as her hide still exists, this is not an orphan.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the last item on its list, the יתום. It also records a disagreement about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says an animal born after its mother died counts as a יתום, because it was never born "under its mother." רבי יהושע disagrees. He holds that if the mother's hide still exists, the animal is not a יתום.

keyTerms.meaning: An orphan; here, an animal born after its mother died
Hide, the skin of the animal
Exists; is still present

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע is not talking about a living mother. Even if the mother was slaughtered, her hide existing is enough for him to say the animal is not a יתום.

phrases.english: And what is an orphan?
Any whose mother died, or that was slaughtered,
and afterward gave birth.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
Even if its mother was slaughtered but the hide exists —
this is not an orphan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the יתום listed in step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A יתום is an animal born after its mother died. רבי יהושע: if the mother's hide exists, it is not a יתום

steps.title: Where Do These Exclusions Come From?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that these animals are left out of מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's list. This sets up the next step, which brings a ברייתא as the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave rules but no verses. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches that each of these animals is excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters derived?

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the biblical source of the משנה in step 7
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse that excludes these animals from מעשר בהמה

steps.title: Each Exclusion Learned From a Verse About Offerings
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns each exclusion from a different phrase in the verse about newborn קרבנות (ויקרא כב:כז).
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: "A bull or a sheep" excludes a mixed breed. "Or a goat" excludes an animal that looks like a different species. "When it is born" excludes a caesarean birth. "It shall be seven days" excludes an animal that is too young. "Under its mother" excludes an orphan.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. Each phrase in the פסוק about קרבנות rules out one type of animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase is read as precise. "Bull or sheep" means a pure species, so כלאים is out. "Is born" means a normal birth, so יוצא דופן is out. "Under its mother" means it had a mother at birth, so יתום is out. This verse speaks about קרבנות in general, so the next step must still connect it to מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; introduces a ברייתא
To exclude
An animal that looks like a different species from its parents

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"A bull or a sheep" — to exclude a crossbred animal,
"or a goat" — to exclude a look-alike,
"when it is born" — to exclude one born by caesarean,
"then it shall be seven days" — to exclude one too young,
"under its mother" — to exclude an orphan.

steps.triggerLanguage: דתנו רבנן שור או כשב פרט לכלאים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא כב:כז excludes each category through a specific phrase

steps.title: Linking Tithe and Offerings Through the Word "Under"
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה uses a גזירה שוה on the word תחת. The exclusions of קרבנות apply to מעשר, and the טרפה exclusion of מעשר applies to קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל, son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, says: Here it says "under the rod," and there it says "under its mother." Just as there all these categories are excluded, so too here. And just as here a טרפה is excluded, so too there.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and connects the verse about קרבנות to מעשר בהמה. Both verses use the word תחת, "under."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in step 10 was about קרבנות, not מעשר. The shared word תחת links the two passages, so the exclusions move from קרבנות to מעשר. The link also works in reverse: "passes under the rod" excludes a טרפה from מעשר, since a טרפה cannot walk through on its own, so a טרפה is also excluded from קרבנות. This completes the source for the full list in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning a law from a word that appears in two places in the תורה
"Under the rod"; the tithe verse, where animals pass under the counting stick
Here / there; the two verses being compared
These categories

steps.whatToRemember: The word תחת links מעשר and קרבנות in both directions. מעשר takes the five exclusions from the קרבנות verse, and קרבנות takes the טרפה exclusion from the מעשר verse.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the משנה's list of animals excluded from מעשר matches the list for קרבנות, including טרפה.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka, says:
It is stated here: "under the rod,"
and it is stated there: "under its mother."

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן — פְּרָט לְכׇל הַשֵּׁמוֹת הַלָּלוּ,
phrases.english: Just as there — all these categories are excluded,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן — פְּרָט לְכׇל הַשֵּׁמוֹת הַלָּלוּ.
phrases.english: so too here — all these categories are excluded.
And just as here — a tereifa is excluded,
phrases.notes: A טרפה cannot "pass" under the rod on its own.

phrases.english: so too there — a tereifa is excluded.

steps.triggerLanguage: נאמר כאן תחת השבט ונאמר להלן תחת אמו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the derivation of step 10 from קרבנות to מעשר בהמה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A two-way גזירה שוה on תחת applies the קרבנות exclusions to מעשר and the טרפה exclusion to קרבנות
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All five categories in the משנה are excluded from מעשר בהמה through the גזירה שוה of תחת

steps.title: What does the word 'all' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה's word 'הכל' comes to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'all animals enter the pen.' What is the word 'all' meant to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices the wide word 'הכל' at the start of the משנה and asks what extra case it is meant to bring in. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes no word in a משנה is extra. If the משנה could have just listed the exclusions, the word 'הכל' must be there to include some case we might have thought was left out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Everything / all.' A wide word that the גמרא reads as including extra cases.
'To include what?' The standard question about an extra, inclusive word.

phrases.english: "All" — to include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the opening word of the משנה in step 7 after the source discussion in steps 9-11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which extra case the word 'הכל' in the משנה includes.

steps.title: A ברייתא: animals unfit for the מזבח are still tithed
steps.stepSummary: 'הכל' includes the ברייתא's list of animals that are unfit as קרבנות but still enter the pen for מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include what the Rabbis taught: an animal that mated with a person, an animal a person mated with, an animal set aside for idol worship, an animal that was worshipped, an animal given as a harlot's payment, an animal given in exchange for a dog, a טומטום, and an אנדרוגינוס. All of these enter the pen to be tithed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'הכל' includes eight kinds of animals. All of them are unfit for the מזבח, yet all of them still go into the pen for מעשר בהמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is surprising. In step 11 we learned that the קרבנות exclusions carry over to מעשר through the גזירה שוה of תחת. These animals are all unfit as קרבנות, yet the ברייתא says they are still tithed. That tension is what the גמרא will challenge in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that had relations with a person (as the active or the passive party).
An animal set aside for idol worship / an animal that was itself worshipped.
An animal given as payment to a harlot / an animal given in exchange for a dog. Both are banned from the מזבח.
An animal whose gender cannot be seen / an animal that has signs of both genders.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up this list with the משנה's five exclusions. The משנה's five (כלאים, טרפה and the rest) do NOT enter the pen. The ברייתא's eight DO enter the pen, even though they are unfit for the מזבח.

phrases.english: To include that which the Rabbis taught:
An animal that mated with a person, and one that a person mated with,
and one set aside for idol worship, and one that was worshipped,
and a harlot's payment, and the price of a dog,
and a tumtum, and a hermaphrodite —
all of them enter the pen to be tithed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'הכל' includes animals that are unfit for the מזבח (because of עריות, עבודה זרה, אתנן, מחיר, טומטום and אנדרוגינוס) but still enter the pen for מעשר.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: טומטום and אנדרוגינוס are not tithed
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יהודה, quoting רבי שמעון, says טומטום and אנדרוגינוס do not enter the pen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס do not enter the pen to be tithed.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion within the same ברייתא disagrees about two items on the list. It says the two animals of unclear gender are left out of מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון agrees about the other six animals but not about these two. The dispute is only about the two animals whose gender is unclear.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In the name of.' Shows that one sage is quoting another.
'Do not enter the pen.' In other words, they are not part of the tithing count.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
A tumtum and a hermaphrodite
do not enter the pen to be tithed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting view inside the same ברייתא, limited to two of the eight animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, טומטום and אנדרוגינוס are left out of מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: Either way, our תנא seems inconsistent
steps.stepSummary: If our תנא learns the גזירה שוה of תחת from קדשים, these animals should be left out too. If he does not, where does he get his own five exclusions?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, as for our own תנא: if he learns 'תחת'-'תחת' from קדשים, then these animals should also not enter the pen. And if he does not learn it, where does he get these exclusions from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the תנא of our משנה with a two-sided problem. Neither choice seems to work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: he uses the גזירה שוה. Then everything unfit for the מזבח should be unfit for מעשר, so the ברייתא's eight animals should not be tithed either. Option two: he does not use the גזירה שוה. Then he has no source for excluding מחוסר זמן, יתום and the rest from מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Our תנא.' The author of the משנה we are learning.
'Learns / derives.' Used here for deriving a law through the גזירה שוה.
'From where does he know it?' A request for a source.

phrases.english: And our tanna,
if he derives "under"-"under" from sacrificial animals —
these too should not [enter the pen],
and if he does not derive it —
from where does he know these [exclusions in the mishna]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the ברייתא in step 13 seems to clash with the גזירה שוה of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא of our משנה, who leaves out five kinds of animals yet includes animals that are unfit for the מזבח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided problem. If he uses the גזירה שוה, all animals unfit for the מזבח should be left out. If he does not use it, his own five exclusions have no source.

steps.title: He does learn the גזירה שוה, but the תורה treats these animals as blemished
steps.stepSummary: The תנא does use the גזירה שוה. But the תורה calls these animals 'corrupt' and counts that as a מום, and blemished animals are tithed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he does learn the גזירה שוה. But the Merciful One included these animals, as it is written: 'because their corruption is in them, a blemish is in them; they will not be accepted for you.' And the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: wherever 'corruption' is mentioned, it refers only to sexual sin and idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that our תנא does use the גזירה שוה. It explains that these animals fall into a different group: they count as blemished animals, and blemished animals do go into the pen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts 'משחתם' (their corruption) right next to 'מום' (blemish). This teaches that corruption is a kind of blemish. The school of רבי ישמעאל teaches that 'השחתה' always means עריות or עבודה זרה. So animals ruined by עריות or עבודה זרה count as בעלי מומין, and the תורה itself includes blemished animals in מעשר. That is why the גזירה שוה does not exclude them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Really / actually.' Signals that the answer keeps the first option of the question.
'The Merciful One (the תורה) included them.' The פסוק specifically brings them in.
'Corruption.' A word that refers to sexual sin and idol worship.
A blemish that makes an animal unfit for the מזבח.
'The school of רבי ישמעאל.' Teachings from his study hall.

steps.confusionAlert: The animals are still unfit for the מזבח. The point is only that their unfitness belongs to the 'blemish' group. That group is tithed, unlike the משנה's five exclusions.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why disqualifications from the מזבח split into two groups. Some carry over to מעשר through the גזירה שוה. Blemish-type disqualifications do not carry over.

phrases.english: Actually, he does derive it,
but these the Merciful One included,
as it is written: "Because their corruption is in them,
a blemish is in them; they will not be accepted for you",
and the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Anywhere that "corruption" is stated,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא דְּבַר עֶרְוָה וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
phrases.english: it refers only to a matter of sexual sin and idol worship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15 by taking its first option.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-categorization: these animals count as blemished, and a separate source includes blemished animals in מעשר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every animal unfit for the מזבח should be left out of מעשר because of the גזירה שוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה שוה applies, but animals tainted by עריות or עבודה זרה count as בעלי מומין, and those enter the pen.

steps.title: Two פסוקים prove that 'corruption' means עריות and עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: The flood פסוק links השחתה to sexual sin. The פסוק about graven images links it to עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sexual sin, as it is written: 'for all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth.' Idol worship, as it is written: 'lest you act corruptly and make for yourselves a graven image, the form of any figure, the likeness of male or female.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the teaching of רבי ישמעאל's school with a פסוק for each meaning of 'השחתה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the flood, 'השחית... דרכו' describes sexual corruption. In ספר דברים, 'תשחיתון' is tied directly to making idols. With both meanings proven, the reading of 'משחתם' in step 16 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter of forbidden sexual relations.
A carved idol (graven image).
Forms of the root שחת, 'to corrupt.'

steps.whatToRemember: Animals unfit for the מזבח because of עריות or עבודה זרה are called 'corrupt', and corruption counts as a מום. Blemished animals are tithed. So these animals enter the pen even though the גזירה שוה of תחת carries the other קרבנות exclusions over to מעשר.

phrases.english: Sexual sin — as it is written:
"For all flesh had corrupted
its way upon the earth",
Idol worship — as it is written:
"Lest you act corruptly and make for yourselves a graven image,
the form of any figure,
the likeness of male or female."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the teaching of רבי ישמעאל's school quoted in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That 'השחתה' refers to עריות and עבודה זרה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית ו:יב (the flood) and דברים ד:טז (graven images).

steps.title: The rule: sin disqualifies only where a blemish disqualifies
steps.stepSummary: Because the תורה counts 'corruption' as a kind of מום, sexual sin and עבודה זרה disqualify an animal only where a מום would. A מום does not disqualify מעשר, so these sins do not disqualify it either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wherever a blemish disqualifies an animal, a sexual sin or idol worship also disqualifies it. Wherever a blemish does not disqualify, a sexual sin or idol worship does not disqualify either. A blemish does not disqualify this tithe animal, as the פסוק says, 'He shall not inquire whether it is good or bad, nor shall he exchange it.' So a sexual sin or idol worship does not disqualify it either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer it started in Step 16. It turns the link between 'corruption' and מום into a general rule and applies that rule to מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 said the תורה calls these animals 'corrupt' and treats that like a מום. Here the גמרא draws the result: the 'corruption' disqualification can only reach as far as a מום reaches. The פסוק of מעשר says not to check whether the animal is good or bad, so a מום does not disqualify it, and these sins do not either.

keyTerms.meaning: A physical blemish that normally makes an animal unfit for the מזבח
A matter of sexual sin
Idol worship
'He shall not inquire whether it is good or bad.' This is the מעשר פסוק showing that blemished animals are tithed.

steps.whatToRemember: Sexual sin and עבודה זרה work like a מום. They disqualify only where a מום disqualifies. Since a מום does not disqualify מעשר, animals involved in these sins still enter the pen.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how our תנא can learn the גזירה שוה of תחת from קדשים and still include these animals in מעשר. Their exclusion from קדשים depends on the rules of מום, and those rules do not apply to מעשר.

phrases.english: And wherever a blemish disqualifies it,

phrases.aramaic: דְּבַר עֶרְוָה וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה פּוֹסְלִין בּוֹ,
phrases.english: a matter of sexual sin or idol worship disqualifies it;
phrases.notes: This works because the פסוק puts 'corruption' next to 'blemish'.

phrases.english: and wherever a blemish does not disqualify it,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין דְּבַר עֶרְוָה וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה פּוֹסְלִין בּוֹ,
phrases.english: a matter of sexual sin or idol worship does not disqualify it.
And this tithe animal, since
a blemish does not disqualify it,
as it is written: 'He shall not inquire whether it is good or bad,'
'nor shall he exchange it'
a matter of sexual sin or idol worship
also does not disqualify it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from Step 16, using the meaning of השחתה that Step 17 proved.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting principle: the disqualification depends on the rules of מום
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the תנא learns תחת from קדשים, every animal unfit for קדשים should also be left out of מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sexual sin and עבודה זרה disqualify only where a מום does. מעשר is not disqualified by a מום, so these animals are tithed.

steps.title: Sorting each animal on the list into sexual sin or idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that each animal on the ברייתא's list belongs to one of the two groups: sexual sin or עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: An animal that mated with a person, or that a person mated with, falls under sexual sin. An animal set aside for idol worship, or actually worshipped, falls under idol worship. A prostitute's payment falls under sexual sin. The price of a dog is compared by the פסוק to a prostitute's payment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the list from the ברייתא. It shows that every animal there fits into one of the two groups the rule covers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from Step 18 only covers sexual sin and עבודה זרה. So the גמרא confirms that every case on the list belongs to one of these two groups. מחיר is not a sexual sin by itself, but the פסוק puts it next to אתנן, so it follows the same rule.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that mated with a person, or that a person mated with
An animal set aside for idol worship, or one actually worshipped
An animal given as payment to a prostitute
An animal given as the price of a dog
It is compared by the פסוק (a הקש)

phrases.english: An animal that mated with a person, or that a person mated with: a matter of sexual sin.
An animal set aside for idol worship, or one that was worshipped: idol worship.
A prostitute's payment: a matter of sexual sin.
And the price of a dog is compared to a prostitute's payment.
phrases.notes: דברים 23:19 mentions both in the same פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule of Step 18 to each item on the ברייתא's list from Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every animal on the list is a case of either sexual sin or עבודה זרה. מחיר is included through its הקש to אתנן.

steps.title: Why the תנא includes טומטום and אנדרוגינוס
steps.stepSummary: The list also includes טומטום and אנדרוגינוס, which are neither sexual sin nor עבודה זרה. The תנא holds that each of these is simply a doubt between male and female.
steps.simpleTranslation: A טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס: the תנא holds that each one is a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last items on the ברייתא's list. These do not fit the 'corruption' rule, so they need a separate reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These animals have no sin connected to them, so the rule from Step 18 does not help here. The תנא's reason is different: such an animal is not a separate kind of creature. It is really either male or female, we just do not know which. Since it is one or the other, it still enters the pen.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose sex organs are covered, so we cannot tell if it is male or female
An animal with both male and female organs
He holds (this introduces someone's reasoning)
A doubt or uncertainty

steps.confusionAlert: Both the תנא here and רבי שמעון בן יהודה in the next step say the same words: 'ספיקא הוא.' They agree these animals are a doubt. They disagree only about whether the תורה's rule against doubtful-gender animals in קדשים carries over to מעשר.

phrases.english: A tumtum and a hermaphrodite:
he holds that each is a doubt (between male and female).
phrases.notes: It is not a separate kind of creature, so it is tithed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes explaining the ברייתא's list. These last items need a reason other than the 'corruption' rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case: the animal is a doubt between male and female, not a separate kind of creature
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think a טומטום or אנדרוגינוס is a separate kind of creature, and so should be left out.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a doubt between male and female, and so the תנא includes it in מעשר.

steps.title: Why רבי שמעון בן יהודה leaves out טומטום and אנדרוגינוס
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יהודה also holds these animals are a doubt. But the תורה requires a definite male or a definite female for קדשים. He carries that rule over to מעשר through the גזירה שוה of תחת תחת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says they do not enter. He holds it is a doubt. The Merciful One excluded doubts from קדשים: only a definite male or a definite female is accepted, not a טומטום or an אנדרוגינוס. For מעשר too, he learns 'under' and 'under' from קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the other opinion from Step 14. It shows why רבי שמעון בן יהודה keeps these animals out of the pen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree these animals are a doubt between male and female. In קדשים, the תורה requires a 'זכר' or 'נקבה' that is certain, so doubtful animals are left out. רבי שמעון בן יהודה carries this rule over to מעשר through the shared word תחת, so in his view these animals do not enter the pen.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One (the תורה) excluded
A definite male and a definite female
A teaching drawn from the same word appearing in two places
'Under.' This word appears in both the קדשים section and the מעשר section, and it is the link for the גזירה שוה.

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree a טומטום or אנדרוגינוס is a doubt. The question is whether the rule that קדשים needs a 'definite male or female' carries over to מעשר. רבי שמעון בן יהודה says yes, through תחת תחת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the real difference between the two opinions. Both opinions use the גזירה שוה in some way, but the תנא of the ברייתא does not let this particular exclusion from קדשים carry over to מעשר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says (they do not enter the pen).
phrases.notes: This quotes the opinion from Step 14.

phrases.english: He holds that it is a doubt,
and the Merciful One excluded doubts with regard to sacrificial animals:
a definite male or a definite female,
but not a tumtum or a hermaphrodite.
For the tithe too, he derives
'under' and 'under' from sacrificial animals.
phrases.notes: This is the גזירה שוה that links מעשר to קדשים.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר קָסָבַר סְפֵיקָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the other opinion, set against the תנא's reasoning in Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Source-based: the exclusion in קדשים carries over through the גזירה שוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a טומטום is really male or female, one might think it should be tithed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה excluded doubtful-gender animals from קדשים. Through תחת תחת, the same exclusion applies to מעשר.

steps.title: A ברייתא: all animals are tithed except crossbreeds and a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that every animal enters the pen for מעשר except כלאים and טרפה. It gives this in the name of רבי אלעזר ברבי יהודה, who quotes רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: All animals enter the pen to be tithed, except a crossbred animal and a טרפה. These are the words of רבי אלעזר ברבי יהודה of the village of Bartota, who said it in the name of רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that lists which animals are left out of מעשר בהמה. According to this opinion, only two kinds are left out: כלאים and טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר בהמה is done by bringing the animals into a pen and letting them pass out one by one, and every tenth animal is holy. This ברייתא says almost every animal goes in. Only a crossbreed and a טרפה are kept out. This short list is the starting point for everything that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: The pen where the animals are gathered to be counted for tithing
To be tithed, meaning counted for מעשר בהמה
An animal born from two different species, for example a goat and a sheep
An animal with a fatal physical defect

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
All animals enter the pen to be tithed,
except for a crossbreed and a tereifa,
these are the words of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yehuda
of the village of Bartota,
who said it in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַכֹּל נִכְנָסִין לַדִּיר לְהִתְעַשֵּׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After discussing the גזירה שוה of תחת תחת with רבי שמעון בן יהודה, the גמרא brings another ברייתא that deals with which animals are excluded from מעשר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only כלאים and טרפה are excluded from entering the pen for מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא adds three more excluded animals
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא reports that he heard from רבי יהושע that three more animals are excluded: יוצא דופן, מחוסר זמן and יתום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: I heard from him that an animal born by caesarean section, an animal that is not yet old enough, and an orphan are also excluded.
steps.whatsHappening: Within the same ברייתא, רבי עקיבא quotes רבי יהושע with a longer list of excluded animals. He adds three cases to the two that the first opinion gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three of רבי עקיבא's cases are animals that may not be brought as קרבנות. יוצא דופן is an animal born by caesarean. מחוסר זמן is an animal less than eight days old. יתום is an animal whose mother died at its birth. So רבי עקיבא's version treats מעשר like קדשים on these points, which sets up the גמרא's next question.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal born through the side of its mother, by caesarean section
An animal that has not yet reached the age of eight days
An orphan animal, whose mother died at or before its birth

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said:
I heard from him (from Rabbi Yehoshua)
that also an animal born by caesarean section
and one lacking time (under eight days old), and an orphan are excluded.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: אֲנִי שָׁמַעְתִּי הֵימֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to the list in step 22, giving a second version of רבי יהושע's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא's report, יוצא דופן, מחוסר זמן and יתום are also excluded from מעשר.

steps.title: Either way, the first opinion seems inconsistent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the תנא קמא a two-sided question. If he learns תחת תחת from קדשים, he should also exclude רבי עקיבא's three cases. If he does not, he has no source for excluding כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the first תנא: if he learns the word 'under' and 'under' from קדשים, then these three should also not enter. And if he does not learn it, it makes sense for a טרפה, since it is written 'whatever passes under the rod', which excludes a טרפה because it cannot pass. But from where does he know to exclude כלאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first opinion in the ברייתא by trapping it between two choices. Neither choice seems to fit his short list of only כלאים and טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Choice one: if he uses the גזירה שוה of תחת תחת to compare מעשר to קדשים, then every animal unfit for קדשים should be excluded. That would include רבי עקיבא's three cases, yet he does not exclude them. Choice two: if he does not use the גזירה שוה, טרפה is still excluded from the פסוק itself ('passes under the rod'). But nothing in the מעשר פסוק excludes כלאים, so where does that exclusion come from?

keyTerms.meaning: The first opinion stated in a ברייתא or משנה
He learns, meaning he derives a law through a גזירה שוה
It makes sense / granted (introduces the part that is not a problem)
The rod used to count the animals for מעשר
From where does he know this?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sources. טרפה is excluded by the מעשר פסוק itself ('passes under the rod'). כלאים can only be excluded by comparing מעשר to קדשים through תחת תחת. That difference is the whole point of the question.

phrases.english: And the first tanna, what does he hold?
If he derives 'under' and 'under' from sacrificial animals,
then these too should not enter the pen,
phrases.notes: Refers to רבי עקיבא's three cases, which are unfit for קדשים.

phrases.english: and if he does not derive it,
granted, a tereifa is excluded,
since it is written: 'Whatever passes under the rod' (Leviticus 27:32),
which excludes a tereifa, since it does not pass,
but a crossbreed, from where does he know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the logic behind the תנא קמא's list in step 22, using רבי עקיבא's additions from step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא קמא's ruling that only כלאים and טרפה are excluded
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma. If he uses the גזירה שוה, his list is too short. If he does not use it, he has no source for כלאים.

steps.title: Answer begins: he does learn the גזירה שוה, but יוצא דופן is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תנא קמא does learn תחת תחת from קדשים, which is how he excludes כלאים. It then starts to explain why יוצא דופן is still not excluded. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, he does learn the גזירה שוה. And regarding an animal born by caesarean section...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks the first side of the dilemma: the תנא קמא does use the גזירה שוה. It is now setting up an explanation of why רבי עקיבא's cases, starting with יוצא דופן, are still included. That explanation comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Choosing the גזירה שוה solves the כלאים problem, since כלאים is unfit for קדשים and so is also unfit for מעשר. What remains is the other side of the question: why are יוצא דופן and the other cases not excluded too? The גמרא begins with יוצא דופן, and its reason is still to come.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / really (introduces the true position in an answer)

phrases.english: Actually, he does derive the verbal analogy,
phrases.notes: This explains how he excludes כלאים.

phrases.english: but with regard to an animal born by caesarean section —
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma of step 24 by choosing its first side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks one side of the dilemma and then explains away the problem with that side
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Using the גזירה שוה would force the תנא קמא to exclude every animal unfit for קדשים, including יוצא דופן.
steps.terutzMaskana: He does use the גזירה שוה, which is why כלאים is excluded. יוצא דופן (and the other cases) must have a special reason to stay included, and that reason is explained next.
